notes.note: Re-checked after the review-round turnHandlers change: attachment adoption moved to hooks/orchestration/recordedAttachments.ts (called from handleTurnStartedEvent), a recorded attachment with a blobRef now drops the bubble's inline data URL and seeds the sent bytes into the bounded attachment object-URL cache, sent bytes carry over only on name+type+decoded-size match, and the unkeyed legacy fallback now skips rows that already have a turnId. The map's claims still hold: line ~4028 (an explicit turn.started.clientTurnId matching an authored bubble is the settle evidence; a heuristic unkeyed match is not retirement evidence) is unchanged and the new !turnId guard only narrows the heuristic; line ~1402 (references resolved on demand through the attachment route) is unchanged. No prose names the new helper module; no edit needed.

Checked recorder.ts startReplayCapture: initialChat now strips data: URLs from file parts of messages and the streaming message (name, type and blobRef kept), leaving the live chat untouched. Added one sentence to the capture paragraph saying the initial state keeps attachment names, types and references but never inline bytes. The 16 MiB / 20,000-frame limits, coverage, redaction-by-default and import validation claims are unchanged (tape-validation accepts the descriptor-only parts; tape-file.test covers capture, strip and round-trip validity).

Checked FilePartPreview's change against GET /api/attachments/:ref (Attachments section ~2850): the route contract, octet-stream/nosniff response, client-applied declared type and 404 chip behavior are unchanged. The client change only reads an already cached object URL for a reference on first render (the cache key, ref plus declared type, moved to attachment-object-urls as attachmentObjectUrlKey) and the cache can be seeded with bytes the sender already holds; the route is still what a chip without cached bytes fetches. No edit needed.

Checked the Chat attachments section against the FilePartPreview / turn.started change. Storage, retention, reclaimed-chip and the transcript's byte-budgeted reference reads are unchanged. Added one sentence: the sending browser's own chips skip the /api/attachments fetch for the turn it just sent, because at turn.started the client drops its inline copy and caches the sent bytes under the recorded reference (recordedAttachments.ts, seedAttachmentObjectUrl). No variable or default changed.
